cards.front: What are reflexive verbs and why are they common in sports?
cards.back:
Reflexive verbs describe actions the subject does TO or FOR itself.

In sports, many actions are self-directed:
entrenarse — to train (oneself)
lesionarse — to injure (oneself)
cansarse — to get tired
prepararse — to get ready
calentarse — to warm up
cards.grammarNote: Reflexive verbs are formed with reflexive pronouns (me, te, se, nos, os, se) placed before the conjugated verb or attached to infinitives/gerunds.

cards.back:
yo        → me
tú        → te
él/ella   → se
nosotros  → nos
vosotros  → os
ellos     → se
cards.grammarNote: The reflexive pronoun must match the subject. 'Me entreno' (I train myself), 'se entrena' (he/she trains himself/herself).

cards.front: entrenarse (to train / to work out) — present tense
cards.back:
yo me entreno
tú te entrenas
él/ella se entrena
nosotros nos entrenamos
vosotros os entrenáis
ellos se entrenan
cards.grammarNote: entrenarse is a regular -ar reflexive verb. 'Nos entrenamos cada semana' = We train every week.

cards.back:
yo me lesiono
tú te lesionas
él/ella se lesiona
nosotros nos lesionamos
vosotros os lesionáis
ellos se lesionan
cards.grammarNote: If you specify the body part, add it with the definite article: 'Me lesioné la rodilla' (I injured my knee).

cards.back:
yo me canso
tú te cansas
él/ella se cansa
nosotros nos cansamos
vosotros os cansáis
ellos se cansan
cards.grammarNote: cansarse = to become tired. Bean se cansa rápido en el sendero. (Bean gets tired quickly on the trail.)

cards.back:
yo me estiro
tú te estiras
él/ella se estira
nosotros nos estiramos
vosotros os estiráis
ellos se estiran
cards.grammarNote: Contrast: 'Estiro las piernas' (I stretch my legs — transitive) vs. 'Me estiro' (I stretch — reflexive, no object named).

cards.front: prepararse (to get ready / to prepare oneself) — present tense
cards.back:
yo me preparo
tú te preparas
él/ella se prepara
nosotros nos preparamos
vosotros os preparáis
ellos se preparan
cards.grammarNote: 'Me preparo para el torneo' = I prepare myself for the tournament. Compare with 'Preparo mi mochila' (I prepare my backpack — not reflexive).

cards.front: calentarse (to warm up) — present tense (stem-changing e→ie)
cards.back:
yo me caliento
tú te calientas
él/ella se calienta
nosotros nos calentamos
vosotros os calentáis
ellos se calientan
cards.grammarNote: calentarse is stem-changing (e→ie) except in nosotros/vosotros. 'Nos calentamos antes del partido' = We warm up before the game.

cards.back:
yo me siento
tú te sientes
él/ella se siente
nosotros nos sentimos
vosotros os sentís
ellos se sienten
cards.grammarNote: 'Me siento cansado después del entrenamiento' = I feel tired after the workout. sentirse describes internal states.

cards.back:
1. Before a conjugated verb:
   Me entreno todos los días.

2. Attached to an infinitive:
   Voy a entrenarme / Me voy a entrenar.

3. Attached to a gerund:
   Estoy entrenándome. / Me estoy entrenando.
cards.grammarNote: Options 2 and 3 each have two valid word orders. Both are equally correct — choose whichever feels natural.

cards.front: Translate: Jeffrey gets tired after two hours of cycling.
cards.back: Jeffrey se cansa después de dos horas de ciclismo.
cards.grammarNote: se cansa is the él/ella form of cansarse. 'de ciclismo' = of cycling; no article needed after 'de' here.

cards.front: Translate: I don't want to injure myself before the tournament.
cards.back: No quiero lesionarme antes del torneo.
cards.grammarNote: The pronoun is attached to the infinitive: quiero + lesionarme. Alternatively: No me quiero lesionar — both are correct.

cards.front: Translate: We train together every Tuesday.
cards.back: Nos entrenamos juntos todos los martes.
cards.grammarNote: nos is the nosotros reflexive pronoun. 'todos los martes' uses the definite article for recurring days.

cards.front: Reflexive vs. non-reflexive: entrenar vs. entrenarse
cards.back:
entrenar (non-reflexive) = to coach/train someone else
El entrenador entrena al equipo.
(The coach trains the team.)

entrenarse (reflexive) = to train yourself
Jeffrey se entrena todos los días.
(Jeffrey trains every day.)
cards.grammarNote: Many verbs can be used with or without the reflexive pronoun, with a shift in meaning. The reflexive adds a 'self' meaning.

cards.front: Translate: She injured herself during the race.
cards.back: Ella se lesionó durante la carrera.
cards.grammarNote: se lesionó is the ella preterite of lesionarse (regular -ar). The reflexive pronoun se stays before the verb.
